title: Introduction to std::string_view
recap: std::string_view, provided by <string_view>, gives inexpensive read-only access to existing character data without owning or copying that data. This makes it a strong default for read-only string parameters.

A std::string_view parameter can accept a C-style string literal, a std::string, or another std::string_view. Passing the view by value is cheap and the function must not use it to modify the underlying text.
objectives: Define a cheap read-only std::string_view function parameter.
Call one function with a string literal, std::string, and std::string_view.
Avoid a std::string copy in a read-only reporting function.
Include the correct headers for both string types.
warnings: Passing std::string by value creates an unnecessary owning copy.
A std::string_view provides read-only access and does not extend an argument's lifetime.
std::string_view does not implicitly convert to std::string, so a by-value std::string parameter cannot accept every required call.
challenge: Repair printLabel() to accept one inexpensive read-only std::string_view parameter. Keep the three calls that pass a string literal, an owned std::string, and another std::string_view, producing the exact deterministic report without input or string copies in the function parameter.
hints: The current std::string by-value parameter owns a new copy and cannot directly accept the final view argument.
Include <string_view> and change only printLabel's parameter type to std::string_view.
Leave all three calls in place; each argument type can initialize the same read-only view parameter.
